cases.prompt: You are the main session described in the input file. Write your reply to the owner exactly as you would send it. Then list any message you send to a thread as `Mail to <build>/<box>:` followed by the full text in a fenced text block. Do not run anything; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Open decisions come first, numbered, owner-before (D4) ahead of D2, each with a recommendation (even the spend item) and its default
The applied default D3 is reported as applied, not re-asked
What the owner can click now (the dev signup URL) is included; the long status is not relayed

assertions.name: digest-quality
rubric: Each open decision carries a recommendation, not only the options
The 20-line catalog-api status is summarised in at most one line or left out
The order is: open decisions, then defaults applied, then what the owner can click

cases.prompt: You are the main session described in the input file. Write your reply to the owner exactly as you would send it, then list every message you send and every command you run, in order: each message as `Mail to <build>/<box>:` followed by the full text in a fenced text block, each command in a fenced bash block. Do not run anything; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: The owner is told a message cannot compact another session; the thread is rotated instead
Both threads are rotated before the overnight absence, the idle shopfront-web one included: ROTATE goes to each, and each thread.sh rotate runs only after that thread's STATUS: rotating arrives
After the rotations, both threads are told the owner is away until 09:00 and that defaults apply at their deadlines

assertions.name: rotation-quality
rubric: The reply explains in one or two sentences why /compact cannot be sent and what happens instead
Both threads are rotated before the overnight absence, the idle shopfront-web one included, and the reply mentions that in at most a clause
thread.sh rotate is described as waiting for each thread's STATUS: rotating, not run immediately after ROTATE
The away steer goes to the threads after rotation and says defaults apply at their deadlines and owner-before items wait
The reply to the owner is short

cases.prompt: You are the main session described in the input file. Write your reply to the owner exactly as you would send it, then list every message you send, command you run and file you edit, in order: each message as `Mail to <build>/<box>:` followed by the full text in a fenced text block, each command in a fenced bash block, each edit as `Edit <path>:` with the change. Do not run anything; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: The steer goes to the threads it affects: shopfront-web for signup and the typo, shopfront-api to park eval-harness
The main session does not fix the typo itself
The owner gets a one-line confirmation

assertions.name: routing-quality
rubric: No lane work happens in the main session: no edit, no subagent started for the build
Each thread gets one message with only what concerns it
The reply to the owner confirms in one or two lines what was routed where

cases.prompt: You are the main session described in the input file. Write your reply to the owner exactly as you would send it, then list every message you send and every command you run, in order: each message as `Mail to <build>/<box>:` followed by the full text in a fenced text block, each command in a fenced bash block. Read the input file, but do not run commands; everything you need is in it.
expected_behavior: The owner is told that shopfront waits on a permission prompt in herdr workspace shopfront and what it asks, and a herdr notification is raised; MAIN neither answers the dialog nor prompts that thread
shopfront-web's screen shows no dialog, so it is rung with one fixed line pointing at its mail; no task text is typed into its pane
Both builds' waits are started again in the background

assertions.name: rearms-both-waits
assertions.pattern: (?s)mail\.sh wait shopfront/main.*mail\.sh wait shopfront-web/main|mail\.sh wait shopfront-web/main.*mail\.sh wait shopfront/main

assertions.name: wake-quality
rubric: The owner is told which workspace to answer and what the prompt asks, in a line or two
The dialog in shopfront is left for the owner: MAIN neither answers it nor prompts that thread
shopfront-web is rung with one fixed line pointing at its mail, because its screen showed no dialog; no task text is typed into its pane
Both waits are restarted in the background

cases.prompt: You are the main session described in the input file. Write your reply to the owner exactly as you would send it, then list every message you send and every command you run, in order: each message as `Mail to <build>/<box>:` followed by the full text in a fenced text block, each command in a fenced bash block. Read the input file, but do not run commands; everything you need is in it.
expected_behavior: With local landing and the owner's go-ahead, MAIN runs thread.sh integrate shopfront, and thread.sh close shopfront either now (the archive keeps the pending diff) or once the owner has answered about the diff
The agents/researcher.md diff is not applied: the owner approved merging, not that change, so MAIN asks about it
No hand-made git merge, worktree removal or branch deletion

assertions.name: finish-quality
rubric: integrate runs through thread.sh; close runs through thread.sh after it, either now or deferred until the owner answers about the diff (the archive keeps the diff either way)
The agents/researcher.md diff is shown or summarised and put to the owner for approval, not applied
The reply is short and tells the owner what was merged where
